summary: H.R. 10692, the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, repeals certain provisions of Public Law 119-21 that previously restricted health-related tax credits for certain lawfully present individuals. The bill restores premium tax credits for lawfully present individuals, establishes a special rule for low-income lawfully present individuals who are ineligible for Medicaid due to their alien status, and allows states the option to increase the maximum household income for Basic Health Program eligibility from 200 percent of the poverty line to a percentage between 200 and 250 percent.

affected_groups.effect: Their eligibility for the premium tax credit is restored by repealing previous restrictions.
affected_groups.group: Lawfully present individuals in the United States

affected_groups.effect: They are treated as applicable taxpayers with household income equal to 100 percent of the poverty line for the purpose of receiving the premium tax credit.
affected_groups.group: Lawfully present individuals with household income at or below 100 percent of the poverty line who are ineligible for Me

affected_groups.effect: States are given the option to increase the maximum household income threshold for Basic Health Program eligibility up to 250 percent of the poverty line.

key_provisions: Repeals section 71301 of Public Law 119-21 to restore the allowance of the premium tax credit for lawfully present individuals.

Provides a special rule for lawfully present taxpayers with household incomes at or below 100 percent of the poverty line who are ineligible for Medicaid because of their alien status, treating them as applicable taxpayers for the premium tax credit.
Applies the premium tax credit restoration for certain low-income lawfully present individuals to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

Grants states the option to raise the maximum household income threshold for Basic Health Program eligibility to a percentage between 200 percent and 250 percent of the poverty line, effective for plan years starting on or after January 1, 2027.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10692, the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, repeals certain provisions of Public Law 119-21 that previously restricted health-related tax credits for certain lawfully present individuals. The bill restores premium tax credits for lawfully present individuals, establishes a special rule for low-income lawfully present individuals who are ineligible for Medicaid due to their alien status, and allows states the option to increase the maximum household income for Basic Health Program eligibility from 200 percent of the poverty line to a percentage between 200 and 250 percent.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal health insurance tax credit rules and state program eligibility limits for specific lawfully present non-citizens. Because the text does not quantify the number of people affected or the overall budgetary impact, its broad economic and societal significance cannot be determined from the source text alone.
